test_cases.label: Test Case B -- NODE_OVERLOAD HIGH escalation (CONTROL-PLANE VALIDATION, NOT an IoT test)
test_cases.method: Direct lambda:Invoke of the EXISTING, DEPLOYED SentinelGridRemediationTrigger Lambda with a hand-crafted DetectionResult (detected=true, fault_type=NODE_OVERLOAD, severity=HIGH). Exercises the real Planner->CheckAutomaticRemediation->Escalate path exactly as a genuine detection would from that point onward. The ONLY synthetic element is the input's origin (this script, not a live telemetry reading through the Analyzer).
test_cases.why_control_plane_not_iot: Confirmed by direct code inspection of lambda_functions/anomaly_detector/detector.py's NUMERIC_FIELD_SPECS/_check_numeric_field: the 'overload' band for every subsystem's overloadable field always yields exactly Severity.MEDIUM -- there is no telemetry value fault_injection/overload.py could ever produce, and no detector rule, that yields NODE_OVERLOAD at HIGH or CRITICAL severity. Forcing this via real telemetry is impossible without inventing a new detector rule, which this step explicitly must not do.
test_cases.anomaly_persisted_note: Correctly NONE -- SentinelGridAnomalyEvents is written by the Anomaly Detector Lambda, which this test deliberately bypassed. This is expected, not a defect.
test_cases.result: PASS -- control-plane escalation path (Planner decision, no Executor/Verifier invocation, RecoveryEvents ESCALATION_REQUIRED, NodeState ESCALATION_REQUIRED, UnresolvedFaultCount incremented) fully validated. Explicitly NOT evidence that real IoT telemetry can produce a HIGH-severity NODE_OVERLOAD classification -- it cannot, under the current detector rules.

test_cases.label: Test Case D -- SENSOR_DROPOUT
test_cases.limitation: fault_injection/faults.py's SensorDropoutFault.blocks_publishing() suppresses publishing entirely for its target node while active -- no telemetry payload of any kind reaches SQS/the Consumer/the Analyzer, so the Lambda pipeline is never invoked and no detection is possible via this fault type as currently implemented. The detector (lambda_functions/anomaly_detector/detector.py's _check_status_dropout / _check_data_container / _check_missing_fields) DOES contain logic that would classify an explicit dropout SIGNAL (status != 'ONLINE', or missing/empty data) as SENSOR_DROPOUT -- but the existing SensorDropoutFault never produces such a signal; it only stops publishing. Per Step 46's explicit instruction not to invent a new methodology to force a fault to be exercisable, this test case was not run live. Missing-heartbeat/absence-based detection was not exercised because the deployed pipeline has no stateful heartbeat-timeout mechanism, and the existing fault injection mechanism for this fault type produces no in-band signal the stateless, per-message detector could act on.
test_cases.result: NOT TESTED -- limitation documented, no code change made

test_cases.label: Test Case E -- NETWORK_PARTITION
test_cases.limitation: fault_injection/faults.py's NetworkPartitionFault.blocks_publishing() also suppresses publishing entirely, identical to SensorDropoutFault -- no telemetry reaches the pipeline. detector.py's own _check_network_partition_hook explicitly documents itself as 'inert, forward-looking': it only fires if a payload carries an explicit network_status field set to PARTITIONED/UNREACHABLE, and its own comment states 'today's simulator never sets it, so this path is not exercised by real output.' Confirmed by code inspection: no code path in fault_injection/ or simulator/ ever sets a network_status field on published telemetry. Per Step 46's explicit instruction, no new heartbeat/network-state detector or fault-injection signal was built to force this test.
test_cases.result: NOT TESTED -- limitation documented, no code change made

detection_summary.note: n=4 is a small controlled functional sample, not a statistically meaningful accuracy measurement. Case B is a control-plane test (not a detection test) and is excluded from this detection-accuracy count.

false_positive_summary.note: False-positive rate not statistically demonstrated -- this is a single ~5-minute window with a 4-node cohort, not a sustained or large-population observation. See Step 38 for separate, larger (500-node) normal-path evidence.
